reuse.why: Keeps calling getDateWithSkippedWeekend for the move case, but the new skip rule is not put in that helper (or a shared one); each site writes its own daily-frequency check and weekend filter.

duplication.why: The 'skipWeekend && frequency is daily' decision and the isWeekend filtering with over-fetch are written separately in getNextDate, getUpcomingDates and schedule-template.

placement.why: Part of the rule is in shared getNextDate, but getUpcomingDates and the budget template re-decide it in the server layer, and the template relies on passing movesWeekend as noSkipWeekend to trigger getNextDate's skipping.

scope.why: Edits are confined to the weekend-handling paths, the parser data, a test and a release note.

maintainability.why: Three diverging implementations (take 14 vs count*4+14, a convoluted empty-result fallback, an inverted boolean reuse of noSkipWeekend) make the rule hard to change consistently.

bypasses_abstraction.where: schedules/app.ts getUpcomingDates filters weekend days itself instead of going through getNextDate/getDateWithSkippedWeekend; schedule-template computes its own movesWeekend flag.

disguised_duplication.where: skipsWeekendDays (shared/schedules.ts getNextDate, schedules/app.ts getUpcomingDates) and movesWeekend (budget/schedule-template.ts) are the same daily-frequency decision under different names and polarities.

one_place.where: The daily-skip rule is decided in shared/schedules.ts getNextDate, server/schedules/app.ts getUpcomingDates and server/budget/schedule-template.ts createScheduleList separately.
